title: Follow the primary task to its result
purpose: A clear interface earns its hierarchy by helping someone finish a job. Test the outcome, including the recoverable failure, rather than the presence of decorative components.
expected: A named action produces its intended result; a refusal preserves input and explains the next useful step.
limit: Example labels and routes must match your product. This verifies a workflow; it does not establish visual quality.

title: Stress the layout with real content
purpose: Responsive design is a negotiation between content, priority, and available space. Use narrow widths and awkward data to reveal what the layout has been assuming.
expected: At 320, 768, and 1440 CSS pixels, primary actions remain usable; the document does not overflow horizontally. Intentionally scrolling tables need separate inspection.
limit: No overflow is necessary but insufficient. Screenshots and task testing must confirm meaningful order and readable content.

title: Make focus follow the interaction
purpose: A pointer screenshot cannot reveal where keyboard users are stranded. Follow focus into a dialog, through its controls, and back to the invoking action.
expected: The dialog receives focus, Escape dismisses it, focus returns to its trigger, and every action has a visible keyboard focus indicator.
limit: A dialog may intentionally focus a heading instead of its first field; adapt the expectation to the content and documented focus decision.

title: Check semantics, then inspect meaning
purpose: The accessibility tree should communicate the same action and structure as the pixels. Pair an automated scan with a direct reading of labels, order, and live feedback.
expected: No violations in the scanned state; labels describe actions and results are announced without unnecessary interruptions.
limit: Requires existing axe dependency. A zero-violation scan is not an accessibility conformance claim.

title: Measure color in its actual role
purpose: Color supports meaning only when the foreground remains distinguishable from its actual composited background. Evaluate text, controls, focus, and semantic states separately.
expected: WCAG AA text contrast is at least 4.5:1, or 3:1 for qualifying large text. Relevant control boundaries and state indicators require 3:1 under the non-text criterion and its exceptions.
limit: Do not round a failing ratio into a pass. Large text is at least 18pt regular or 14pt bold; inactive controls have specific exceptions.

title: Verify motion and its quiet equivalent
purpose: Animation should explain state, location, or causality. Its reduced-motion version must communicate the same result without relying on travel or repeated movement.
expected: The result is understandable with reduced motion, repeated actions do not overlap, and exits do not strand focus or leave invisible hit targets.
limit: State assertions do not assess motion quality. Inspect normal motion, interruptions, rapid reversal, and reduced motion directly.

title: Exercise the component’s complete state model
purpose: A beautiful default state says little about slow, missing, or refused work. Build states from the resource lifecycle and give each a useful next step.
expected: Loading is distinct from empty; failures preserve context; retries cannot duplicate an operation; disabled controls explain what is missing.
code:
Use your existing fixture or request-interception seam to produce:

loading   → stable geometry, clear pending feedback
empty     → reason for absence + useful first action
success   → result appears + feedback names the completed action
error     → speakable cause + retained input + recoverable next action
partial   → available content remains useful + missing data is named
long data → large counts, long names, translated labels, missing media

For each relevant state:
  capture the viewport and accessibility tree;
  perform the primary action using keyboard and pointer;
  record the actual result and recovery, not just a screenshot.

Network race: submit twice while pending. Observe one intended operation.
Do not claim that a disabled button alone proves backend idempotency.
limit: A state inventory is evidence planning, not the skill. Choose the states that the component can actually enter.

title: Give gestures a discoverable alternative
purpose: Swiping and dragging can reduce effort for fluent users, while hiding the action from everyone else. Preserve the same operation through an ordinary visible control.
expected: The same action is available without a complex path gesture or drag. Targets meet the applicable size criterion; common 44px comfort targets are a design choice, not WCAG AA’s blanket minimum.
limit: A desktop emulated viewport is not touch-device verification. Irreversible actions need an appropriate recovery or confirmation decision.
